pl-l3d38c3-d1e115.summary: Sets out what must be seen: what a lie is, what lying is, and whether every lie is a sin, and why.

pl-l3d38c3-d1e118.summary: Defines a lie, after Augustine, as a false signification by speech with intent to deceive: there must be something false said with intent to deceive, the liar's proper evil being to have one thing hidden in the breast and another ready on the tongue.
claims: A lie requires falsehood and intent to deceive.

pl-l3d38c3.summary: Sets out the questions to be treated: what a lie is, what lying is, and whether every lie is a sin, and why. Following Augustine, a lie is a false signification by speech with intent to deceive: what is said must be false and said with intent to deceive, the liar having one thing shut in his breast and another ready on his tongue.
claims: A lie is a false signification with intent to deceive.
A lie requires both falsehood and intent to deceive.
